tool: audit-context-building (dossier D: verify-then-accept, and the paths a key or server address takes through the CLI)
skill: trailofbits/skills plugins/audit-context-building (pinned); run as a subagent writing one record per function to review/context/functions/ (core__actions__verify__*, core__actions__pull__*, workflow__pull__*, workflow__clone__*, core__actions__clone__*, core__actions__commit__*, cli__CLI__Main__*, cli__CLI__Vault__*; 44 records)
run: 2026-10-11; the dossier names no vulnerabilities by design; its `nothing found` assumptions and its reconstruction of the verify-then-accept order are turned into claims below
the_rule_as_implemented: a local named ref or a baseline is written at exactly three places (writable pull Step__Pull__Fetch_Missing._accept, read-only pull Step__Pull__RO__Checkout, Vault__Sync._fetch_branch_for_switch), each after the rewind guard and then require_signatures; clone verifies (step 9) before registration, checkout and the key writes; the one write before any check is the server's index bytes on clone

findings.title: on clone, an index the client cannot parse (a non-gate failure) degrades to a synthesised single-branch index with no features: a host serving a garbled index to a newcomer switches signatures-required off for that clone
findings.status: VULN (reproduced: clone succeeded with a garbled host index, local features empty; fixed: TM-F35; the withheld-index residual stays under TM-R29 with its own test)
evidence: Step__Clone__Download_Index L34-77, L89-112, L114-154: index bytes saved before decrypt (L55); parse failure other than the client-too-old gate → synthesised index, no features
the register says a fresh clone 'takes whatever the host serves' (TM-R29 note); 'nothing' is also something the host can serve

actor: A1 alone (no read key needed to garble bytes); the clone then accepts unsigned history from the same host (A1 still needs A3 to author commits that decrypt, so the chain is A1 for the policy and A3+A1 for the forgery)

proposed.fix: an index that exists on the host but does not parse refuses the clone (name the host); only an absent index (a vault that never had one) synthesises
proposed.test: Fixed: clone of a vault whose index bytes are random under the read key refuses; control: a legacy vault with no index still clones

findings.title: the rewind guard's UNKNOWN verdict (offline, or more than 50 commits of lineage the clone cannot connect) is treated as not-rewound: the pull proceeds and merges with an empty base
evidence: classify L50-62: FORWARD / REWOUND / UNKNOWN; callers refuse REWOUND and exceptions only
Step__Pull__Fetch_Remote_Ref._guard_rewind L15-56: API errors inside _fetch_commit_chain return connected=False (no exception) → UNKNOWN → proceed; commit_fetch_limit defaults 50 (Vault__Sync__Pull)

a host (with a read-key holder's help, TM-R01) that replaces the branch with an unrelated chain longer than 50 commits is not a rewind to the guard; the policy check still runs, so under signatures-required the chain must be signed by a key that decrypts (which TM-R01 allows)

proposed.fix: UNKNOWN refuses unless --accept-rewind, with the message naming why (offline / limit); raise the default limit for the connectivity walk, which is local objects plus fetched commits
proposed.test: Fixed: an unrelated 60-commit head is refused as 'cannot connect to the last accepted head'

findings.title: the writable pull accepts the named ref and baseline in step 4, before the dirty-tree guard and the merge in step 5: a pull refused for a dirty working copy or stopped by conflicts has already moved the clone's notion of the remote head
findings.status: CLEARED (reproduced the refusal: a dirty-tree refusal left remote_heads.json unchanged and the working copy intact; the dossier read the step order, the guard runs before the accept)
evidence: _accept L29-44 (server's raw ref bytes + baseline, plain open, no reflog); execute L46-121 order: policy → fetch → missing-blob refusal → accept

proposed.fix: accept after the dirty guard passes (the fetch can stay where it is; only the ref and baseline writes move), or write the baseline only when the merge completes
proposed.test: a dirty-tree refusal leaves named ref and remote_heads.json unchanged

findings.title: _fetch_branch_for_switch swallows any exception from reading the server ref (undecryptable bytes, a 403) and returns as if offline; pull distinguishes these (F9), switch does not
evidence: L173-211: `except Exception: return` at L202; the head is a raw json str; no index refresh before the policy check on this path (open question in the dossier)

proposed.fix: reuse pull's classification of the ref read (offline vs undecryptable vs refused)

findings.title: clone falls back to limit=1 (head only) when the recorded policy anchor is not among the downloaded objects, so history under the head goes unchecked on a full clone in that case
findings.status: VERIFY (can the anchor be absent legitimately on a full clone? a partial / range clone yes; a full clone only if the host withheld it)
evidence: execute L24-71, _anchor_commits L73-83; register TM-R30 covers the no-anchor case for pre-0.21 vaults, not an anchor withheld by the host

proposed.fix: a full clone whose index names an anchor it did not receive refuses (the host withheld an object the policy depends on)

findings.title: vault format: min_client can go down (format never does); a write-key holder or a replayed index lowers the floor that keeps old clients out of writes
evidence: cmd_vault_format L1828-1852 + Vault__Sync__Format.set_format L17-67: format never down, min_client 'not newer than self', nothing stops a lower value; TM-R26 relies on min_client

proposed.fix: min_client never goes down without --force, mirroring the format rule

findings.title: cmd_info prints the passphrase, the full vault key, the read key and a web URL carrying the bare vault key in its fragment; cmd_derive_keys prints the write key in bare hex; cmd_clone prints the read key after every full clone
findings.status: KNOWN (TM-R14), with two items the register does not name: the write key on stdout (derive-keys) and the read key after every clone
evidence: cmd_info L1704-1804; cmd_derive_keys L2166-2191; cmd_clone L208-326

proposed.fix: a --quiet / no-key form for clone; derive-keys behind an explicit --show-write-key; info prints the key only with --show-key (it has show-key already)

findings.title: remote add / set-url / the remote setup prompt send the stored token to a user-typed URL for a health check before that URL is recorded
findings.status: VERIFY (low: the user typed the URL; the risk is a typo that sends the token to the wrong host, with no --no-health-check by default)

proposed.fix: health-check without the token (the API's health endpoint needs none), or confirm the host before sending it

findings.title: vault ignore --apply writes its removal commit unsigned, silently, when the clone's .pem is missing; commit warns in the same case
evidence: cmd_vault_ignore L1609-1653 + Vault__Ignore__Apply.apply L19-85 vs Vault__Sync__Commit._load_signing_key L20-30 (stderr warning)

findings.title: RuntimeError text from the API is printed verbatim and includes the server's response body; Safe_Str validation errors echo the offending value (a mistyped key on argv is echoed back)
findings.status: VERIFY (low; the token and key headers are masked in API errors)
evidence: run L822-897 → _print_friendly_error L1010-1067; Vault__API._api_error masks headers; Safe_Str errors include the value (osbot-utils behaviour)

findings.title: load_public_key never checks data['type'] == 'public'; a legacy private-key file under bare/keys decrypts and import then raises, which reads as no-key
findings.status: CLEARED (fails closed into no-key, which the policy refuses)

findings.title: the policy start anchor is read from the server-merged index, deliberately not pinned (TM-R29/R30); when the anchor is not local, policy_start is empty and pre-policy commits between the held head and the anchor are checked (fails closed)
findings.status: CLEARED (the direction of the failure is the safe one; documented in the register)

findings.title: the per-command server pin exempts clone, init, create and remote (the env var steers them by design and init records it); a one-off --base-url on pull is persisted by resolve_base_url
findings.status: KNOWN (TM-F22 design); the persistence of a one-off flag is the same shape as AC-C-005
